title: The AI Guard boto3 hook for Amazon Bedrock: before-call and after-call scanning, what the content walkers read, block styles, and what is not scanned

prose.text: The boto3 hook attaches to the botocore event system of a bedrock-runtime client, so every model call through that client is scanned, including calls a framework makes. {{registration}} {{prompt-before-signing}}

checks.do: Whether the application streams (ConverseStream or InvokeModelWithResponseStream); for those only the prompt is scanned.
Whether a protected client is the only path to Bedrock; other clients, processes and raw HTTPS calls are not covered.
Whether the request carries assistant turns or tool specifications built outside this client; those reach the model unscanned.
That the hook is constructed only with the options its code accepts; apply_masked_data from the README raises TypeError.

registration.statement: `protect_client` (one client) or `protect_session` (every bedrock-runtime client later created from the session) registers before-call and after-call handlers for Converse, ConverseStream, InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream under fixed unique IDs, so protecting twice registers one set; other clients, processes and raw HTTPS calls are not covered.

quotes: Other clients, other processes, other languages, and raw HTTPS calls to Bedrock are not covered

prompt-before-signing.statement: The prompt is scanned in before-call; a block returns before botocore signs or sends the request, so nothing reaches AWS or is billed.

quotes: A blocked prompt is stopped **before the request is signed or sent**: nothing reaches AWS, nothing is billed.
return self._blocked("prompt", blocked_verdict, transaction_id, operation, model_id)

prompt-coverage.statement: For Converse calls the prompt leg scans the system prompt and every user-role message; assistant-role turns and the tool specifications in `toolConfig.tools[].toolSpec` are sent to the model unscanned.

quotes: """(text, opaque): the system prompt plus EVERY user-role message, not just
Assistant-role turns and tool specifications are not scanned here.
as is `toolConfig.tools[].toolSpec` (name, description, input schema), which Bedrock renders into the model's context.

block-walker.statement: The content walker is an allowlist: it reads text, guardContent text, toolUse name and arguments, toolResult text, JSON and search results, reasoning text, searchResult passages and citation text; documents, images, video, audio, redacted reasoning and any unrecognized block are flagged opaque, except a `cachePoint` holding only `type` and `ttl`.

quotes: if members and all(key in ("type", "ttl") for key in members):
# document / image / video / audio -- and, fail-closed, everything else.
return [], True                 # redactedContent is an encrypted blob

Both legs walk the content blocks the same way: `text`, `guardContent` text, `toolResult` text and JSON, `toolUse` (tool name plus serialized arguments -- model-emitted arguments are text the application is about to act on),
`reasoningContent` reasoning text, `searchResult` passages, and `citationsContent` answer and cited source text.

invoke-dialects.statement: For InvokeModel the prompt is taken from the messages dialect, from Cohere's `message` with `chat_history`, `documents` and `tool_results`, or from `inputText` or `prompt`; a body in no known dialect, or one that is not JSON, is scanned whole as raw text.

quotes: if isinstance(body.get("messages"), list):        # messages dialect (incl. amazon nova)
for key in ("inputText", "prompt"):               # titan / llama, mistral
prompt = raw           # unknown dialect: scan the whole body
for turn in body.get("chat_history") or []:   # every turn, not just the newest

prompt-opaque-blocks.statement: On the prompt leg any opaque content blocks the call when `on_unscannable` is `"block"` (the default), even when the request also carries text.

quotes: note="content that cannot be inspected as text")
Unscannable content follows the `on_unscannable` posture **on the prompt leg** (blocked by default;
The request leg applies the posture to both cases.

response-only-text-sent.statement: The response leg scans the assistant text with direction OUT and sends only that text; the prompt the hook stores for the response leg is not included in the request.

quotes: text = contents.get("prompt") if leg == "prompt" else contents.get("response")

response-opaque-ignored.statement: The response leg discards the walker's opaque flag: a reply with no extractable text follows `on_unscannable`, but a reply that mixes text with a block the walker cannot inspect (such as a document, an image or an unrecognized block) is scanned on its text alone.

quotes: A response that carries no extractable text at all follows `on_unscannable`; one that mixes text with a block the walker cannot inspect is scanned on its text.
**The response leg blocks on "no text", not on "some opaque content".**
documents, images, video, audio, redacted reasoning, and any block shape it does not recognize are flagged unscannable rather than skipped

stream-response-skipped.statement: For ConverseStream and InvokeModelWithResponseStream only the prompt is scanned; the streamed response is still on the wire when after-call fires, so the hook logs a skipped-stream line and returns without scanning it.

quotes: For the two streaming operations the response is still on the wire when `after-call` fires; only their prompt leg is scanned.

aws-errors-pass.statement: An AWS error response (a parsed `Error` or an HTTP status of 300 or more) is not scanned: the hook steps aside so botocore raises the genuine exception (a throttle, auth failure or validation error) instead of masking it with a scan verdict.

quotes: An AWS error (throttle, auth failure, validation error) carries no model output; the hook steps aside so botocore raises the genuine exception instead of masking it with a scan verdict.

block-styles.statement: With `on_block="raise"` (the default) a block raises `AIGuardBlocked`; with `"respond"` the hook returns a well-formed reply instead: a Converse message with `stopReason` `content_filtered`, a JSON body for InvokeModel, or a minimal event stream for the streaming operations, with the verdict under `ResponseMetadata.AIGuard`; a blocked response is replaced the same way.

quotes: `on_block="respond"` delivers a well-formed response instead -- a `content_filtered` Converse reply on either leg, a JSON body for `InvokeModel`, or a minimal valid event stream for the two streaming operations -- whose text states the block, with the verdict attached under `ResponseMetadata.AIGuard`

unknown-options-rejected.statement: The hook accepts only `app_name`, `policy_id`, `session_id`, `app_user`, `on_block`, `on_verdict`, `on_error`, `on_unscannable`, `strict_verdict`, `scan_prompt`, `scan_response` and `timeout`, and raises TypeError for any other option.

masking-option-rejected.statement: Passing `apply_masked_data`, which the README documents for masking, makes `protect_client` or `protect_session` raise TypeError, and the module contains no masking path.
masking-option-rejected.conditions: Follows from the complete option set; a search of the module at the pin finds no other mask handling (the only `masked` occurrence is a log-level label).

readme-invalid-python.statement: The README's configuration example has two bare `policy_id=` lines, so it is not valid Python as written, and one describes the policy ID as an "AI profile UUID" while the module parses it with int().

quotes: policy_id=           # AI profile UUID; name or id must resolve

session-unused.statement: `session_id`, `app_name` and `app_user` are accepted and stored but never used: each call gets a fresh uuid4 transaction ID, and neither the scan request nor the log line carries them.
session-unused.conditions: Rests on a search of the module at the pin: the three attributes are assigned in the constructor and read nowhere. The README promises session correlation and metadata.app_name.

response-context.summary: Whether the response scan carries the prompt as context.

positions.says: The README's sequence diagram shows the after-call scan sending the response with the prompt as context when prompt scanning is on.

quotes: B->>A: after-call: scan response (prompt as context, when scan_prompt is on)

positions.says: The code stores the prompt with the response but sends only the response text.

quotes: text = contents.get("prompt") if leg == "prompt" else contents.get("response")

response-context.impact: Detections that need the prompt beside the response see only the response on this seat; the Lambda decorator and the AgentCore guard do send both.

masking.summary: Whether the boto3 hook can apply AI Guard masking to a response.

positions.says: The README documents apply_masked_data=True: masked text replaces the response's text blocks on mask-and-allow profiles, and InvokeModel gets a replacement envelope.

quotes: apply_masked_data=False,   # masked text replaces the response on mask-and-allow profiles

positions.says: The module's option set has no apply_masked_data and it rejects unknown options.
The Apigee example's architecture note says AI Guard returns a verdict, not a rewritten payload, so there is no masking path.

masking.impact: Following the README's masking setup fails at construction with TypeError. Whether the detection API returns masked content at all is not settled by these examples; the SDK's response model (ai-security.ai-guard.runtime-api:response-fields) lists no masked-content field.
